role: You are a visual educator, motion designer, and Remotion developer.
task: Build a 60-second, 9:16 DataEntropy explainer animation that shows beginners what a common table expression (CTE) is: WITH lets you write the first step of a query up front, give its result a name, and read from it like a table in the second step. Carry one example through the whole video: Rumi, an analyst, wants every customer whose orders add up to more than 500. Deliver complete, editable Remotion code and a rendered MP4.

reference.project: diffusion-video (60-second template) and sql-select-video (the series pilot: table cards, query card, typing, check marks)
take_inspiration_from: Continuous transformations instead of slide changes
Objects moving in response to a question
Labels appearing exactly when their meaning becomes clear
A viewer feeling as though they are discovering the mechanism
reference.originality: Create original artwork, colors, typography, and compositions.

video.audience: Beginners: students and early-career professionals who want practical data skills. Simple, friendly language; every necessary term is explained in plain words in the same scene.
video.structure: The brand guideline's 30-second structure scaled to 60 seconds: hook, problem, explanation, outcome, call to action in the last 6 seconds. 11 scenes, each about 4-6 seconds.
video.style: Clean, minimal vector line-art motion graphics on a white (#FFFFFF) background with off-white (#F8F7FC) content cards and generous whitespace. Deep navy (#172554) for headlines, labels, table outlines and cell text; brand violet (#6D4AFF) for SQL keywords, the active table part, check marks and arrows; electric purple (#8B5CF6) for motion accents; soft lavender (#C4B5FD) only as filled bands, pills or glows placed behind navy text or a darker outline. Tables are white rounded cards with a bold 5px outline, a navy name tab and bold navy text. Text that is not picked turns pale gray (#D6D2E0) and is never the focus. Every line, arrow, connector and outline is a bold 4-6px stroke with rounded endpoints in deep navy, brand violet or electric purple. Rounded corners 8-20px, soft low-opacity violet-tinted shadows. No dark backgrounds, no red, orange or neon colors. At most three focal points per scene.
video.typography: Inter (fallback Arial, sans-serif). Headlines weight 700, at least 54px, deep navy, left-aligned at the top of the safe area, maximum two lines and 12 words, with one or two key words in brand violet. Table text and labels at least 32px on screen, deep navy. SQL code in JetBrains Mono, at least 32px on screen.
video.subtitles: Enabled in the lower-middle safe area. Inter SemiBold white (#FFFFFF) text inside a solid rounded deep navy (#172554, 88% opacity) box; maximum 2 lines and 7 words per line; word-group reveal synchronized with the voiceover; key words in soft lavender (#C4B5FD).
video.safe_area: Top 10%, bottom 18%, left 7%, right 7%. Headlines, subtitles, logo and CTA stay inside x 76-1004px and y 192-1574px. Headline zone y 192-400; world content y 400-1390; subtitle bar bottom edge at y 1560.
video.voiceover: Voice en-US-AvaNeural (the diffusion explainer's voice), per-line pace fitted with tools/fit_vo_pace.py. 135-155 words per minute while speaking. Few commas, because each comma adds a pause.
video.mobile_readability: Use large text, short labels, and generous spacing. Keep essential content inside platform-safe margins.

central_visual.description: TOP LEFT: the table 'orders' (customer, amount), a white card with a bold 5px deep navy outline. TOP RIGHT: the temporary 'totals' table with a bold 5px brand-violet outline, and under it the result table. BELOW: a wide query card with a bold 5px navy outline.
central_visual.interaction_effect: Step one makes the order amounts travel into the totals table and add up. Step two tests the totals rows and sends the ones that pass to the result. When the query ends the totals table fades away.
central_visual.camera: One continuous space, held steady so the long query stays readable.

timeline.visual: A white table card named 'orders' with a bold 5px deep navy outline draws itself: columns customer and amount, six rows with three customers mixed together. Headline with '500 in total' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: Who spent more than 500 in total?
timeline.voiceover: Rumi wants every customer who spent more than five hundred in total.

timeline.visual: Beside the table two white step chips with bold navy outlines are revealed one after the other: '1. add up each customer' and '2. filter the totals', joined by a bold 5px brand-violet arrow. Headline: 'two steps' in brand violet.
timeline.voiceover: That takes two steps. First add up each customer. Then filter the totals.

timeline.visual: Below, a wide query card with a bold 5px navy outline draws itself and types a nested query with brand-violet keywords; the inner query sits in the middle on a soft lavender band, wrapped by the outer one. Headline: 'hard to read' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: A query in a query is hard to read
timeline.voiceover: You can put one query inside another. But it gets hard to read.

timeline.visual: The lines of the query slide out and a new version slides in: 'WITH totals AS (' on top, the same inner query under it, then the final query below. The name 'totals' sits on a soft lavender pill. Headline: 'WITH' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: WITH gives a step a name
timeline.voiceover: WITH lets you write step one first and give it a name. That is a CTE.

timeline.visual: Beside the orders table a card with a bold 5px brand-violet outline and the tab 'totals' draws itself. Each order's amount travels across in a white chip with a bold violet outline to its customer's row, where a bold navy total counts up: Arif 700, Mina 650, Rafi 250. Headline: 'totals' in brand violet.
timeline.voiceover: Step one adds up the orders into a small table called totals.

timeline.visual: A white chip with a bold brand-violet outline and navy text 'temporary' is revealed beside the totals tab, and a bold 5px brand-violet outline draws itself around the first four lines of the query, the part that defines totals. Headline: 'inside this query' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: It lives only inside this query
timeline.voiceover: It is temporary. It exists only inside this one query.

timeline.visual: A soft lavender band spreads behind the last two lines of the query. A band with a bold violet outline steps down the totals rows: Arif and Mina get bold violet check marks and travel into a result table with a bold violet outline, while Rafi fades to pale gray. Headline: 'like any table' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: Step two reads it like any table
timeline.voiceover: Step two reads totals like any other table and keeps the big spenders.

timeline.visual: Two round brand-violet badges with white numbers appear beside the query: 1 beside 'WITH totals AS (' and 2 beside the final SELECT, and a bold 5px brand-violet arrow draws itself down the left side of the card from 1 to 2. Headline: 'top to bottom' in brand violet.
timeline.voiceover: Now the query reads top to bottom, in the order you think.

timeline.visual: The totals card and its 'temporary' chip fade away. The result table with Arif and Mina stays, with a bold violet outline. Headline: 'is gone' in brand violet.
timeline.on_screen_text: Afterwards the step table is gone
timeline.voiceover: When the query ends, totals is gone. Only the answer remains.

timeline.visual: The orders table, the query with its two numbered badges and the result table sit together; a bold 5px brand-violet outline draws itself around the result. Headline: 'small named steps' in brand violet.
timeline.voiceover: So break a big question into small named steps.

timeline.visual: The tables and the query card fade away. The DataEntropy logo's four bars grow upward left to right in brand violet, the wordmark is revealed, and a soft violet glow settles. The tagline is revealed, then one brand-violet CTA button with a white animated arrow: 'Follow DataEntropy'. Hold the final composition for at least two seconds.
timeline.voiceover: Follow DataEntropy for more SQL explained simply.

animation_rules: VISIBILITY ON WHITE: every line, arrow, connector, outline and text must be clearly visible on the white background. Draw them as bold strokes of at least 4px in deep navy (#172554), brand violet (#6D4AFF) or electric purple (#8B5CF6). Use soft lavender (#C4B5FD) only for filled bands, pills or glows behind navy text, never for lines, small dots or text.
No abrupt slide cuts; every scene transforms naturally into the next in one continuous space with a camera.
Animate concepts, not decorative particles. Every animation has a job.
One example carries the whole video. The tables keep their identity and position from scene to scene.

SQL on screen is one short query in a monospace face, typed clause by clause, with keywords in brand violet. Use only syntax that works the same in PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and SQL Server; leave dialect-specific syntax such as LIMIT or TOP off screen.
Rows have no built-in order. Do not say or imply that an answer comes back in table order unless the query has ORDER BY.
All names, cities and amounts are invented illustrative examples.
Explain every necessary term in plain words in the same scene it appears.
Synchronize each label and highlight with its voiceover phrase.
Use deterministic frame-based animation so any frame renders correctly when scrubbing the timeline.
Use the brand easing cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); no rapid flashing, glitch effects or excessive bouncing.
Nothing rises or scales as it appears: card outlines draw themselves and fill in, rows and chips are wiped in from the left.
'Temporary table' is a way to picture a CTE, not a promise about storage: say it 'acts like' a small table that exists only inside this query.
The subquery version must be valid SQL too: a subquery in FROM gets an alias.
A CTE is not saved in the database; show it disappearing when the query ends.
Code in this video is 34px on screen because the inner SELECT line is long.

implementation.graphics: Original SVG and code-generated shapes; no stock footage or paid assets

deliverables: Remotion preview and MP4 render commands
Brief explanation of where to edit text, colors, and timing
quality_check: Render and inspect a still at the key moment of every scene. Fix clipping, overlaps, unreadable labels and any line or text that is hard to see on white. Confirm that each total is the real sum of that customer's orders and that the result holds exactly the customers above the threshold.
